name: nvidia-openshell-ocsf
producer: NVIDIA OpenShell sandbox supervisor, OCSF v1.8.0 JSONL export (/var/log/openshell-ocsf.YYYY-MM-DD.log inside the sandbox), as documented at docs.nvidia.com/openshell
description: The security event log of NVIDIA's OpenShell agent runtime, part of the Open Agent Safety Platform announced 28 September 2026. Every network, HTTP, SSH, process, finding, config and lifecycle event is written as one OCSF object per line, and each allow/deny names the policy rule that decided it. Per NVIDIA's own documentation the file is written inside the sandbox the agent runs in, rotates daily keeping three files, and carries no integrity field, no sequence number and no drop accounting. L0.
_basis: Scored from NVIDIA's public documentation as read on 2026-09-29 (Sandbox Logging; OCSF JSON Export), not from a capture of a running OpenShell. The example logs are constructed record by record from the field lists and examples on those pages. Anything the documentation does not state is recorded below as unstated, and each note ends in the question a capture or NVIDIA's source would settle. Sentry, the BlueField-4 monitor, is not scored: its records, if any, are not documented.

integrity.note: No hash, signature or chaining field is documented for either log file. metadata.uid is described as a unique event identifier, which names an event; it does not bind one record to the next. Question: does OpenShell sign or chain the OCSF file anywhere, or only rely on the SIEM it is shipped to?

loss.note: No sequence number and no record of dropped, rate-limited or suppressed events is documented. Rotation keeps the three most recent daily files and deletes older ones with no in-log record of what was removed, so a day-four export is indistinguishable from a log that began on day two. Question: does the supervisor count events it failed to write, and does metadata.uid carry any ordinal?

coverage.note: Records are emitted for what the sandbox proxy and supervisor observed. Nothing in the log states which network paths, processes or channels the supervisor was able to observe, so traffic that bypassed the proxy leaves no record and no gap. Question: is there a record declaring the supervisor's observation surface for the sandbox?

policy.note: Each allow/deny names the rule that decided it (firewall_rule.name and .type, e.g. github_api / opa), which is more than most agent logs carry. It does not bind the policy's version or digest, and network policy can be updated at runtime without a restart, so a recorded ALLOWED is not tied to the rules as they stood when it was decided. Question: does any record carry a digest of the policy in force?

independence.boundary_statement: The documentation places the OCSF file at /var/log/ inside the sandbox, alongside the agent it records, and describes no control preventing the sandboxed process from writing to or deleting it. It is therefore scored as writable by the audited party until shown otherwise; if the file is in fact written from outside the agent's reach, this entry changes. Question: can a process inside the sandbox write to or delete /var/log/openshell-ocsf.*?
